The accused-applicant has filed the present bail application being aggrieved against the order dated 18.09.2025 passed by the learned Additional Session Judge (Women Atrocities Cases),
District Udaipur in Criminal Misc. Case No.266/2025 (Sanjeev vs. State of Rajasthan), whereby the bail application filed by the accused-applicant under Section 483 B.N.S.S. was rejected.

The accused-applicant is behind the bars, pursuant to the F.I.R. No.205/2025 registered at Police Station Goverdhan Vilas, District Udaipur against the accused-applicant for offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 386, 504 and 506 of IPC.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record.

3. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that the prosecutrix, in her statement recorded under Section 183 BNSS, has admitted to having a consensual relationship with the accused-applicant since the year 2017, however, both the accused-applicant and the prosecutrix were married to other

(Uploaded on 08/10/2025 at 06:16:52 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:44203] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-11755/2025] persons at that time.

Learned counsel further contends that the prosecutrix,
in her statement, also admitted to pressurizing the accused-applicant to divorce his the then-wife and marry her.

Additionally, the prosecutrix was involved with an individual named Jayant, and the accused-applicant had informed her husband about this fact, following which, the FIR was lodged against the accused-applicant.

Moreover, the detailed transcripts of chats between the accused-applicant and the prosecutrix's husband, along with various photographs, clearly indicate that the accused-applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel also Sanjeev vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:44203) on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107704211/
1 asserts that the FIR against the accused- applicant was registered as a consequence of his having informed the prosecutrix's husband about prosecutrix being involved with one Jayant.

He,
therefore, implores this Court to allow the present Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application.

4. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the statement of prosecutrix reveals clear allegations regarding the commission of rape upon her under the pretext of marriage; accordingly, the present case squarely falls within the definition of rape, therefore,
prayed that looking to the gravity of offences committed by the accused-applicant and the potential adverse impact on society in the event of his release, the accused-applicant ought not to be enlarged on bail.

5. Having considered the arguments advanced by both parties and in light of the facts and circumstances of the case, including the prosecutrix's admission of a consensual relationship with the accused-applicant while both were married to other individuals, as (Uploaded on 08/10/2025 at 06:16:52 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:44203] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-11755/2025] well as her admission to having pressured the accused-applicant to marry her post divorcing his wife, and further considering the photographs and detailed transcripts of chats between the accused-applicant and the prosecutrix's husband, this Court, without expressing any opinion on the merits or demerits of the case, is inclined to enlarge the accused-applicant on bail.
6. Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 B.N.S.S. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-applicant; Sanjeev S/o Gattu Lal Barot, arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.205/2025 registered at Police Station Goverdhan Vilas, District Udaipur, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
7.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
(SANDEEP SHAH),J 224-Mrityunjay Rathore/-
